This clears every completed chapter, star, badge, and scripture card, and starts back at Noah\'s Ark. This can\'t be undone. Your child\'s character and sound settings will stay the same.

Bible Adventures does not collect any personal information. We never ask for your child's name, email address, phone number, or location, and the app never requests access to contacts, the camera, or the microphone.

There is no account or sign-in of any kind. All progress is saved in one file on this device only — nothing is sent anywhere else.

The app works fully offline and contains no ads, no in-app purchases, and no chat or messaging with other people.
Tap to hear from your character
Scripture card, locked. Complete %1$s first to unlock.
Help Noah gather the animals and trust God\'s plan.
Stand with young David as he faces a giant with faith, not fear.
Learn what it means to be a good neighbor to everyone you meet.
Watch a small gift multiply into more than enough for everyone.
Stay faithful with Daniel, even when it feels scary to pray.
Help Esther bravely approach the king and save her people from Haman\'s wicked plot.
Courage and speaking up at the right time.
March around the walls of Jericho and trust an unusual plan.
Ride out a stormy sea and discover peace in the middle of fear.
Helped Noah build the ark and gather every animal, two by two.
"And Noah did so; according to all that God commanded him, so he did."
"I have set my rainbow in the clouds, and it will be the sign of the covenant between me and the earth."
Faced a giant with courage and trust in God.

"Then David said to the Philistine, \'You come to me with a sword, with a spear, and with a javelin; but I come to you in the name of Yahweh of Armies, the God of the armies of Israel, whom you have defied.\'"
Stopped to help a stranger in need, just like the Good Samaritan.
"But a certain Samaritan, as he traveled, came where he was. When he saw him, he was moved with compassion,"
Stayed faithful to God through prayer, even when it was risky, just like Daniel.
"My God has sent his angel, and has shut the lions\' mouths, and they have not hurt me, because innocence was found in me before him; and also before you, O king, I have done no harm."
Found the courage to speak up for her people, just like Esther.

"For if you remain silent now, then relief and deliverance will come to the Jews from another place, but you and your father\'s house will perish. Who knows if you haven\'t come to the kingdom for such a time as this?"
Trusted Mordecai\'s wise advice and kept a humble heart, just like Esther.
"Esther had not yet made known her relatives nor her people, as Mordecai had commanded her; for Esther obeyed Mordecai, like she did when she was brought up by him."
Helped Mordecai warn the king of danger, just like a faithful friend.
"This thing became known to Mordecai, who informed Esther the queen; and Esther informed the king in Mordecai\'s name."
Helped gather messengers to warn the city and call people to pray, just like in Esther\'s time.
"In every province, wherever the king\'s commandment and his decree came, there was great mourning among the Jews, and fasting, and weeping, and wailing; and many lay in sackcloth and ashes."
Bravely spoke the truth to save her people, just like Esther.
"Then Esther the queen answered, \'If I have found favor in your sight, O king, and if it pleases the king, let my life be given me at my petition, and my people at my request.\'"
Marched in obedience and trusted God\'s plan instead of using force, just like the people of Israel.

"So the people shouted and the priests blew the trumpets. When the people heard the sound of the trumpet, the people shouted with a great shout, and the wall fell down flat, so that the people went up into the city, every man straight in front of him, and they took the city."
Shared what little he had, and watched it become more than enough for everyone, just like the boy with the loaves and fish.
"Jesus took the loaves, and having given thanks, he distributed to the disciples, and the disciples to those who were sitting down."
You\'ve already solved this puzzle! Tap Next Page to move on, or play it again.
That doesn\'t belong on the ark!
You need to collect something first.
Tap each tool hidden in the picture.
Drag each basket onto a deck — but only if it fits exactly. Some baskets belong on a different deck.
We can obey God, even before it makes sense.
We can keep going, even when a job feels big.
We can trust God to take care of every little thing.
We can feel safe with God, even in a storm.
We can be patient, even when we\'re waiting for good news.
We can trust God, even when we have to wait.
We can thank God for keeping every promise.
We can be faithful in small jobs, even when no one is watching.
We can stay calm, even when trouble looks bigger than us.
We can speak up for what\'s right, even if others feel afraid.
We can be brave just being who God made us to be.
We can trust that God can use small, simple things.
We can be strong, because the battle belongs to God.
We can give God the credit when good things happen.
Flip the cards to match each number with its group of sheep.
David already has one stone. Drop stones to connect four in a row — across, up and down, or on a diagonal — before Goliath does!
You found your stones! David is ready.
Choose a brave response for David.
"The Lord will save me — He is with me!"
"I\'m not afraid, because God is bigger than you!"
"You come with a sword, but I come in the name of the Lord!"
David spoke with quiet, steady faith!
David\'s courage rang out across the valley!
David stood tall, trusting God completely!
Pull back the sling to begin — then let go to hit each rat before it scurries away!
It got away — here comes another one!
David\'s stone. Drag to aim, then let go.
We can notice when someone is hurting, even in unexpected places.
We can choose to stop, even when it\'s easier to walk away.
We can make time to help, even when we\'re busy.
We can be a good neighbor to everyone we meet, not just our friends.
Slide the pieces out of the way to help the Priest/Levite tile reach Jericho.
Well done! Tap me for the next puzzle.
Tap to go to the next puzzle
That\'s what the priest and the Levite did… but we shouldn\'t be like them. When we see someone hurt, we should stop and help.
Drag the joystick to walk the road. Find medical supplies, help the traveler, then reach the Inn.
This is the road the traveler and the Samaritan walked. Let\'s follow it together.
Move the Samaritan — drag in any direction
These bandages and medicine can help someone who is hurt. Look for them along the road!
Robbers hide along this road and may try to steal your supplies. Toss your medical supplies at one to scare it away!
This man was beaten by robbers and left hurt beside the road. Bring him medical supplies to help him.
Throw medical supplies at the bandit
Out of supplies! Retreat and look for more along the road.
Your turn — tap yourself to attack!
He needs medical supplies first — look around for some nearby!
You stopped to help the traveler!
The Samaritan knelt down and bandaged the man\'s wounds.
He gently poured on oil and wine to help him heal.
Then he helped the man onto his own animal to carry him the rest of the way.
We can obey God, even when a new rule makes it risky.
We can keep praying, even when it\'s against the rules.
We can trust God to protect us, even in the scariest moments.
We can see God keep His promises, even after a long, hard night.
We can stay faithful to God, no matter what happens.
Tap a latch to release it. If another latch is in its way, it will get stuck — clear the outer ones first.
That latch is stuck — clear what\'s blocking it first.
Choose what Daniel says as he kneels to pray.
"I will trust you, no matter what happens."
"I am not afraid, because you are with me."
Daniel knelt by his open window and prayed, just as he always did.
Daniel prayed boldly, trusting God completely — even knowing the law.
Daniel\'s prayer rang out through the open window, unafraid.
Solve each problem to draw a ring of the shield around you. Answer wrong and the lions creep closer!
The lions, watching from a distance
The lions, right at the edge of the shield
The lions got too close! Try again.
Use the joystick to race through the maze to the lions\' den.
Move through the maze — drag in any direction
The maze to the lions\' den
Esther was a Jewish orphan raised by her cousin Mordecai. When the king searched for a new queen, she was brought to the palace.
Mordecai gave her wise advice: don\'t tell anyone you\'re Jewish, not yet.
Esther spent months preparing before she would ever meet the king.
Help her get ready by finding everything she needs.
Tap each item to gather it for Esther — some things in the room aren\'t hers.
The king chose Esther, and she was crowned queen of Persia.
She still kept Mordecai\'s secret, just as he had asked.
How should Esther speak to King Xerxes?
The king was pleased with her kindness.
Esther\'s thoughtfulness stood out among everyone in the palace.
Her gentle patience won the king\'s favor.
Esther trusted Mordecai\'s wise advice, even when it meant keeping a secret. Sometimes the bravest thing we can do is quietly obey and wait for the right time.
One day, Mordecai overheard two of the king\'s officers whispering a dangerous plot.
He needed to warn Queen Esther — quietly, without the guards noticing.
The palace courtyard was watched closely, and Mordecai couldn\'t risk being seen carrying a warning note.
Help him slip across the courtyard without a guard spotting him.
Move Mordecai toward Esther — watch where the guard is standing before you step!
A guard noticed! Try again quietly.
Mordecai\'s note reached Esther, who told the king everything — in Mordecai\'s name.
It was written down in the king\'s own royal records.
Mordecai stayed alert and told the truth right away, even when it was risky. Watching out for others and speaking up honestly can protect the people we love.
A proud official named Haman was promoted, and everyone bowed to him — except Mordecai.
Furious, Haman tricked the king into signing a wicked law against Mordecai\'s people, the Jews.
The decree spread to every province of the kingdom, and news of the danger needed to reach everyone.
Complete each row of the puzzle to send out a messenger with the warning.
Tap an empty square, then tap a symbol. Each row and column needs every symbol exactly once.
That symbol is already used in this row or column!
A messenger is on the way!
Word reached every corner of the city — Mordecai tore his clothes and wept bitterly.
Everywhere, the Jewish people fasted, wept, and mourned together.
When danger came, the people didn\'t face it alone — they stood together, prayed, and supported each other. We\'re stronger when we face hard things as a community.
Mordecai sent word to Esther: "Who knows if you have come to the kingdom for such a time as this?"
No one could approach the king uninvited — not even the queen — without risking their life.
"I will go to the king, even if it is against the law."
"I will trust God with my life."
Esther asked everyone to fast and pray for her for three days first.
Esther\'s courage grew as she prepared to approach the king.
Esther chose to risk everything for her people.
Esther asked Mordecai and all the Jews in the city to fast and pray for her for three days.
On the third day, she put on her royal robes and walked toward the king\'s throne room.
Tap each lane in rhythm as the markers arrive, to help Esther find her courage as she walks.
Esther approached the king\'s throne, even though it was against the law to come uninvited.
The king held out his golden scepter — Esther was safe, and he asked what she wished.
Esther risked everything to speak up for her people at just the right time. When we trust God and stay brave, He can use us for good, even when it\'s scary.
The king welcomed Esther and asked what she wished. She invited him and Haman to a banquet.
At the first banquet, Esther waited — she would ask her true request at a second banquet instead.
Esther prepared a beautiful banquet table to welcome the king and Haman.
Help her arrange everything in its place before her guests arrive.
Drag each food to its place on the table.
At the second banquet, the king again asked Esther what she wished — even up to half his kingdom.
This time, Esther was ready to speak the truth.
Help Esther choose her words bravely.
The truth about the plot against her people
Who is really behind the plot?
The king was furious, and Haman\'s own wicked plan was turned back on him instead.
A new decree let the Jewish people defend themselves, and they were saved.
To this day, Jewish people celebrate the festival of Purim to remember how God saved them.
When the moment finally came, Esther spoke the truth clearly and bravely. Speaking up honestly, even when it\'s hard, can protect the people we love.
Joshua led God\'s people to a mighty, walled city called Jericho. Two brave spies went ahead to see the land.
God had a plan to bring the walls down — but it wasn\'t like any battle plan anyone had heard before.
The spies stayed at the house of a woman named Rahab, who lived inside Jericho\'s walls.
Soon, soldiers came looking for them.
Rahab hid the spies and kept them safe, even though it put her in danger.
She hid them on her roof under stalks of flax, then sent the soldiers searching the wrong way, toward the river.
Rahab\'s house was built right into the city wall. Slide the pieces to untangle the rope before the soldiers finish searching.
Rahab lowered the spies by the rope, right through her window in the wall.
She told them to hide in the hills for three days, until the search was over.
In return, they promised to keep her and her family safe — if she tied a scarlet cord in that same window.
God\'s plan didn\'t look like a battle at all. Choose what Joshua and the people will do.
"We will follow God\'s plan, even though it seems strange."
"We will trust God, not our own strength."
"We will obey, one step at a time."
The people marched in silence, trusting God\'s unusual plan.
Joshua led the people forward, trusting God more than swords or shields.
Step by step, the people obeyed exactly as they were told.
God held back the Jordan River so all the people could cross on dry ground.
Joshua chose twelve men, one from each tribe, to carry twelve stones from the riverbed and build a memorial.
Drag the stones onto the monument in order, from the lowest number to the highest.
As the tents went up around the new memorial, the people talked about everything Joshua had led them through.
He had led them safely across the Jordan, just as God promised — and the people trusted him to lead them the rest of the way, toward Jericho.
Jericho\'s gates were shut tight — no one went in or out.
God told Joshua exactly what to do: march around the city once a day, for six days, without a sound.
Tap each lane in rhythm as the footprints arrive, to march one lap around the wall — once for each of the six days. No shouting, no talking, just steady steps.
On the seventh day, God gave one more instruction: march around the city seven times, not just once.
Seven priests would carry seven trumpets — and this time, when the trumpets sounded, the people would shout.
Faster now! Tap each lane in rhythm to complete all seven laps around the wall.
Solve each problem and pick the right answer to sound the next trumpet note.
The trumpets are sounding — now SHOUT! Tap again and again to bring the walls down.
When the walls fell, Rahab tied the scarlet cord in her window, just as she was told.
She and her family were kept safe, exactly as the spies had promised.
\'t fight to bring down the walls — they marched and trusted God\'s plan, even when it seemed strange. When we obey God, He can do things no strength of ours ever could.
A great crowd had followed Jesus into the hills to hear him teach and to be healed.
As the day grew late, the disciples realized there was no food anywhere nearby — and thousands of people were hungry.
Jesus told his disciples to have everyone sit down in groups on the green grass.
So the crowd sat down in neat rows — some in groups of fifty, some in groups of a hundred.
Drag each family into a seating circle — but only if it fits exactly. Some families belong in a different circle.
Jesus asked Philip, "Where can we buy bread for all these people to eat?"
Philip did the math out loud — even two hundred silver coins wouldn\'t buy enough. Andrew went to look through the crowd for anything at all.
Search the crowd for the boy carrying a basket — he might have something to share.
Andrew found a boy in the crowd — and the boy was willing to share exactly what he\'d brought.
"There is a boy here who has five barley loaves and two small fish," Andrew said, "but what good are they for so many?"
Find exactly 5 barley loaves and 2 small fish in the basket — some things in here aren\'t food at all.
The boy has so little, and the crowd is so big. What would you do with your own lunch?
Give everything, even though it\'s not much
Keep a little back, just in case
The boy gave everything he had — and trusted Jesus with the rest.
It\'s natural to want to hold something back — and Jesus still welcomes what we\'re able to give.
Asking Jesus first is always a good instinct — he already knew exactly what he was going to do.
Jesus took the boy\'s five loaves and two fish in his hands.
He looked up to heaven, gave thanks, broke the bread, and gave it to his disciples to hand out to everyone.
Solve each problem and pick the right answer to watch the food multiply.
The disciples carried the food out to the crowd — and it just kept coming.
Everyone ate, and everyone was full. There was more than enough.
Walk out and serve every group of people their share of the bread and fish.
Group of people waiting to be served
Use the arrows to move the basket into the right lane before each leftover lands — gather exactly twelve baskets full.

The boy didn\'t have much — just a small lunch. But he gave it anyway, and Jesus made it more than enough for thousands. When we share what we have, even if it seems small, God can do more with it than we ever could alone.
As evening came, Jesus said to his disciples, \'Let us go over to the other side of the lake.\'
Leaving the crowd behind, they took him along, just as he was, in the boat.
Before they could sail, the boat had to be loaded and ready.
Help load the heaviest things first, so the boat stays steady on the water.
Drag each item onto the boat, heaviest first, so it stays balanced.
Place the item in the boat
Jesus was in the stern, sleeping on a cushion.
A furious squall came up, and the waves broke over the boat, until it was nearly swamped.
Use the arrows to move to wherever the water is pouring in, before it fills the boat.
The storm is fierce and the boat is filling with water. What would you do first?
Grab the oars and row harder!
Cry out to Jesus for help!
Rowing hard is brave — but the storm was far too strong for oars alone.
Holding on tight kept the disciples safe — but the storm still raged on.
Crying out to Jesus was exactly the right instinct — he was there all along.
In all the chaos, the disciples couldn\'t understand how Jesus could sleep through it.
Make your way to the stern to wake him: \'Teacher, don\'t you care if we drown?\'
Use the arrows to make your way across the storm-tossed deck to Jesus.
Jesus got up and rebuked the wind, and said to the waves, \'Quiet! Be still!\'
Say each word the moment it\'s ready, just as Jesus did.
Tap each word the instant it\'s ready — say it just as Jesus did.

The wind died down, and it was completely calm. Jesus asked, \'Why are you so afraid? Do you still have no faith?\' The disciples were amazed, saying, \'Who is this? Even the wind and the waves obey him!\' When life feels like a storm, Jesus is right there with us — and he is always in control, even when we\'re afraid.
Stayed with Jesus through the storm, and watched him calm the wind and the waves with just a word.
"He awoke, and rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, \'Peace! Be still!\' The wind ceased, and there was a great calm."
